az_pirate_wall.blurb: Pirate Wall is a small sport crag in the Midgley Bridge area near Sedona, Arizona. It has five bolted climbs: one very easy line, a pair around 5.7, and a pair at the 5.9 level, one of which stretches to three pitches. The wall is long and faces southeast, with orange rock toward its left end and darker patina toward the right. From the Midgley Bridge trailhead, follow Wilson Canyon trail to the Jim Thompson trail junction, bear left, and walk roughly a quarter of an hour; the wall appears on your right.

az_rehab_wall_the.blurb: The Rehab Wall is a tall, rough-looking crag in the Oasis section of Granite Gardens, in the Granite Dells near Prescott. Its five routes are spread around a west face, a southwest arete and a side that looks south, mixing four sport lines with one trad line from about 5.8 up into the low 5.12 range. The granite is coarse and grainy, but it reportedly cleans up fast. To get there, leave the car in the Granite Gardens lot, cross the creek, follow the trail into the large open field, and look to the right for the wall.

az_dry_gulch.blurb: Dry Gulch is a small trad area within the Oasis section of Granite Gardens, in the Granite Dells near Prescott. It occupies a wide ravine just beyond the tunnel on the Grotto Trail. All five routes are short and gentle for trad: one at 5.5 and four at 5.7, with a couple also used as top-rope. A low-angle pillar with a bolted line is the easiest feature to spot, and the remaining routes are tucked up behind it. The walk starts at the dirt lot, crosses the creek, passes through the big field, then follows the trail through the tunnel.

_expect.name: Son of Broken Rubber (Main Upper Boulder)

az_son_of_broken_rubber_main_upper_bould.blurb: This is a large boulder at Gates Pass, in the Sonoran Desert near Tucson, and is described as probably the best boulder in the zone. Five problems range from an easy V0 through the middle grades, with most falling around V3 to V5. Most lines get morning and midday sun. From the Broken Rubber boulder, follow the main trail south for roughly four to eight minutes; the boulder stands on your right. Bring pads, and watch for jumping cholla and rattlesnakes. The area is called pleasant in the winter months.
